results.fact: Trailhead to Kool-Aid Lake distance: itinerary day 1 (6.5 mi) vs the Kool-Aid Lake waypoint and dist_km (5.5 mi)
results.evidence: Retried with other traverse descriptions and route pages. They consistently give 3.7 mi of trail to Cascade Pass and describe the rest (Mixup traverse, Cache Glacier, Cache Col, descent to the lake) by time rather than distance; a club route page gives 12.0 mi and 4,000 ft trailhead-to-summit round trip, and the row itself also cites 16-17 mi (totalNote) and ~19-20 mi (approach) round trip. No two sources state the trailhead-to-Kool-Aid Lake distance, so neither 5.5 nor 6.5 mi can be confirmed without computing it.

results.fact: Summit-day duration vs. its own timestamped schedule
results.evidence: Still real on the live row: day 2 hours 9 (= summitTimeHrs 6 + descentTimeHrs 3) against a schedule running 2:30 AM to 2:30 PM. No published source gives timings for the Northeast Face itself; the only published times are for the standard East Ridge summit day. Rewriting the clock times would mean inventing a schedule, so nothing is changed.

results.fact: Total gain 4,500 ft is less than the trailhead-to-summit rise
results.evidence: Confirmed real: 4,500 ft is below the ~5,400 ft net rise from the ~600 ft trailhead to the 5,991 ft Main Peak. Published car-to-car gain figures exist only for Main Peak by itself (a club route page gives 5,500 ft; a 2017 party reports over 6,000 ft), and they disagree; neither covers the three-summit traverse with its intermediate drops. Adopting either would be a figure for a different outing, so gain_ft is left for a source that states the traverse total.

results.fact: Total gain/loss: gain_ft 6,000 vs loss_ft 5,500 vs approach '~5,500 ft' on an out-and-back
results.evidence: Retried. A club route page for the Lake Serene / east gully line gives 5,500 ft of gain; a 2017 party on Hourglass Gully itself writes that they did over 6,000 ft of gain to the summit. The two sources disagree in the same way the row does, so there is no two-source figure to make gain_ft, loss_ft, the approach and the approach variant agree on.

results.fact: round-trip distance and gain figures disagree
results.evidence: Retried; a further club route page for the Northwest Ridge gives 8.0 mi and 4,000 ft, adding a fifth distinct figure to the 7.0 / 7.4 / 5.3 / 4.62 mi already found. No two independent sources agree on one distance or gain for this path, so the row is left as is.

Same open question as the Northwest Ridge row (same climbers' path): published round-trip figures are 4.62, 5.3, 7.0, 7.4 and 8.0 mi, with no two independent sources agreeing. dist_km (5.6 km) and the itinerary/variant 5.3 mi RT are both left unchanged.

results.fact: access.permit says 'None required' but the top-level permit field says a free self-issue Wild Sky Wilderness permit or trailhead registration
results.correct_value: No wilderness permit or quota; Northwest Forest Pass (or equivalent) at the Barclay Lake trailhead
results.evidence: The Forest Service's own Wild Sky Wilderness page lists under Passes and Permits only that some trailheads require a recreation pass, and the forest's wilderness-regulations page lists a self-issue permit only for the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. The Barclay Lake hike listing on an independent trail database gives only the Northwest Forest Pass / interagency pass. Both agree no Wild Sky permit or registration exists, matching access.permit, so the top-level permit field is corrected.
